title: Turning 600 discontinued product pages into leads
excerpt: Search traffic was still landing on 600+ product pages for flooring that was no longer sold. Instead of deleting them, each one became a way in: email capture, related products and back-in-stock alerts.

metrics.label: Discontinued product pages turned into lead sources
Independently run stores brought into one CRM and review process

content:
01 · Discover

Traffic with nowhere to go

A site audit showed more than 600 product pages for discontinued flooring that still ranked and still drew visitors from search, but sold nothing. Each visit hit a dead end.

Deleting or blanket-redirecting them would have thrown away rankings the store had already earned, so the pages stayed and got a new job.

03 · Build

A dead end becomes a way in

  • Email capture on every discontinued product page
  • Relevant product recommendations, so visitors find what is in stock today
  • Back-in-stock notifications where a product could return
  • Automated follow-up campaigns for the people who signed up

Previously underused search traffic started turning into qualified leads and sales, and email marketing grew into a real sales channel for the business.

05–06 · Maintain and evolve

Fifteen stores, one view of the customer

Flooring Liquidators runs 15 independently operated locations, each with its own QuickBooks account, customer data and Google Business Profile. I helped design a centralised CRM and lead-management setup that consolidates and segments customer information, automates communication, improves review management across every profile, and gives leadership one view of customer activity and marketing performance.

Alongside · Local SEO

Fifteen locations, found locally

Each store has its own Google Business Profile and location page. I kept the profiles consistent, tied them to their location pages and ran review requests through the CRM, so every store could show up in local results and map listings in its own area.

Alongside · Paid media

Ads brought in-house

Google and Meta advertising moved in-house, with campaign, retargeting and site performance data used to improve audience targeting, landing pages, promotions and conversion rates.
